transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-06-02
Start time: 16:30 PDT
Duration: ~28 minutes
Attendees: Avery Patel (Recruiter), Jordan Lee (Hiring Manager), Priya Singh (Candidate)

Summary:
Brief recruiting screen for Senior Software Engineer role; discussed Priya's background, tech stack, current notice period, compensation expectations, visa/status, and interview loop. Agreed next steps: send take-home exercise and schedule hiring manager interview.

Topics:
- Background & recent projects
- Tech stack (Go, Python, React)
- System design exposure and distributed systems
- Availability & notice period
- Compensation expectations & location
- Interview loop & next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery: Hey Priya, thanks for joining, can you hear us okay?
[00:05] Priya: Yes, hi thanks for having me.
[00:08] Jordan: Hi Priya, Jordan here, hiring manager for the infra team, nice to meet you.
[00:11] Priya: Nice to meet you too.
[00:13] Avery: Quick note, this is just a 20-30 minute screen to go over your background and make sure expectations align, we'll take notes and then we'll follow up with next steps.
[00:20] Priya: Sounds great.
[00:22] Avery: Could you walk us through what you're doing now and the last couple of roles?
[00:27] Priya: Sure, currently I'm at LumenWorks, been there for two years as a Senior Backend Engineer. Mostly building microservices in Go, some Python for data pipelines, and I've been leading a small team of two. Prior to that I was at BrightCloud where I worked on streaming ingestion and a real time feature store, so lots of Kafka, Redis, slightly older stack but.. um, good experience.
[00:48] Jordan: Nice, you said Go primarily — how comfortable are you with systems level work, like performance tuning, memory, GC, that sort of thing?
[00:55] Priya: Yeah, pretty comfortable. In the last role I worked on optimizing our serialization path, we had about 2x throughput improvements after switching to a pooled buffer strategy and fixing a couple GC pressure points, so I did a bunch of profiling with pprof and flamegraphs.
[01:12] Avery: Do you have any direct experience with GPU workloads or model serving? Not required but curious for some infra overlap.
[01:18] Priya: I haven't done GPU infra myself, most of my work was on CPU microservices. I have paired with ML teams to help expose endpoints and set up autoscaling but not low level GPU stuff.
[01:28] Jordan: That's okay, this role is infra-focused but we can mix in infra orchestration, autoscaling, and some work with model-serving teams. Do you have experience with Kubernetes?
[01:35] Priya: Yes, daily. I wrote operators for backup jobs and helped tune HPA thresholds. Might mispronounce but um, Kubernetis? I mean Kubernetes — sometimes I say it funny.
[01:44] (light chuckle)
[01:46] Jordan: Totally. How about languages and testing — you mentioned Python and Go, any TypeScript/React experience?
[01:52] Priya: I have some front-end experience on small dashboards using React and TypeScript, nothing deep but I can read it and do minor fixes. My main depth is backend.
[02:01] Avery: Great. How about large scale systems — have you done distributed caching or KV store work?
[02:06] Priya: Yes, at BrightCloud we ran a sharded Redis cluster and I helped with eviction policies and read routing; at LumenWorks we also used a tiered KV cache for hot paths.
[02:16] Jordan: Sounds relevant. Quick question on interview logistics — what's your current notice period and are there any constraints for start date?
[02:23] Priya: I'm on a two-week notice, can be flexible to extend a little but two weeks is standard.
[02:28] Avery: Are you authorized to work in the US?
[02:31] Priya: Yes, I'm a US citizen.
[02:34] Jordan: Compensation — are you open to telling us a range you're targeting?
[02:38] Priya: I'm looking for base in the 160k-180k range, total compensation obviously depends on equity and bonuses, but that's the base target.
[02:46] Avery: Thanks, that's in line with the range for this band. Any location constraints, remote vs onsite?
[02:50] Priya: Remote is preferred, I'm based in the Bay Area but open to occasional onsite visits.
[02:56] Jordan: Cool. On the technical side, our loop typically includes a take-home coding exercise, a hiring manager interview focusing on system design and leadership, and two technical interviews — one backend focused and one infra/systems. Is that acceptable?
[03:08] Priya: Yes, that's fine. How long is the take-home usually?
[03:11] Jordan: Typically 48-72 hours turnaround but we give a week if you need it. It's a small service design + coding task.
[03:18] Priya: Okay that works.
[03:20] Avery: Anything in your resume you want to highlight that isn't obvious, or any projects you're proud of?
[03:25] Priya: I led a migration from a monolith to a microservice architecture at BrightCloud; we rebuilt a legacy ingestion pipeline into scalable consumer groups in Kafka, that reduced lag by 70%. I also open-sourced a small instrumentation library internally that teams adopted.
[03:40] Jordan: Nice, can you tell me about a time you had a production incident and what you did?
[03:44] Priya: Sure — one time we had a cascading failure from a bad deployment that overloaded our DB replicas. I rolled back, executed a throttling policy at the ingress, worked with on-call DB folks to failover to a healthy replica, then we added circuit breakers and request quota limits to prevent recurrence.
[04:02] Avery: Good. Any questions about the team or culture?
[04:06] Priya: What does success look like in the first six months for this role?
[04:09] Jordan: Good question. We expect by six months you'd be owning an important service, driving reliability improvements, and shipping at least two medium-sized features; collaborating with ML infra for a couple of integrations is likely.
[04:22] Priya: Sounds good.
[04:24] (short pause)
[04:26] Avery: A couple of housekeeping things — do you have any upcoming interviews or offers we should be aware of?
[04:31] Priya: I'm in final stages with one other company but no offers yet.
[04:35] Jordan: Okay that's fine, just helps us prioritize.
[04:37] Avery: For the take-home, acceptable languages are Go, Python, or Java — is that alright?
[04:41] Priya: Yep I can do Go or Python.
[04:44] Avery: Great. Anything else you want to ask about compensation, benefits, or equity?
[04:49] Priya: Not right now, perhaps later. Also curious about interview timing — how soon could panels be scheduled if we move forward?
[04:56] Avery: We can usually schedule the hiring manager loop within a week depending on availability, then the technical interviews within the following 1-2 weeks.
[05:04] Priya: That timeline works for me.
[05:06] Jordan: Quick technical: have you designed systems with eventual consistency or multi-region concerns?
[05:11] Priya: Yes, worked on cross-region replication for a cache tier and designed fallback behavior for stale reads; used vector clocks in a limited system for conflict resolution at BrightCloud.
[05:24] Jordan: Good. Any experience with observability stacks — Prometheus, Grafana, tracing?
[05:29] Priya: Yes, set up dashboards in Grafana, lots of Prometheus metrics, instrumented services with OpenTelemetry for traces.
[05:36] Avery: Okay, quick recap and next steps — we'll send the take-home exercise and an official invite for the hiring manager loop if you are interested. Can you confirm you'll complete the exercise within 72 hours?
[05:47] Priya: Yes, I can do 72 hours.
[05:49] Avery: Perfect. Any final questions?
[05:52] Priya: No, thank you for the time.
[05:54] Jordan: Thanks Priya, looking forward to reviewing your exercise.
[05:58] Avery: I'll follow up with the materials and calendar invite.
[06:01] Priya: Thanks so much.

(End of recording — notes appended)

Notes (recruiter):
- Candidate strengths: strong Go backend skills, experience with Kafka and caching, production incident handling, comfortable with infra/operator tasks.
- Risks: limited GPU/model serving experience, front-end is not a strength (not required).
- Compensation expectation: 160k-180k base; remote Bay Area.
- Availability: 2-week notice; US citizen.

Recap / Next steps (vocal):
- Avery to send take-home and schedule hiring manager loop (Avery/Jordan)
- Candidate to complete take-home within 72 hours
- Update ATS and move to next stage if exercise passes
